subject: plm Mediation with fixed effects in lavaan

messages.author: 883770839c4a1766
messages.subject: plm Mediation with fixed effects in lavaan
parts:
Hi everybody, 

I want to calculate a Mediation in lavaan, struggeling with the topology of my data, which is a classical panel Data (index = ID and time). Up to now, I did some basic regressions with the plm function, where it is possible to control for fixed effects with the model="within" command also the effect="twoways" (which includes time and individual fixed effects). The reression looks like this:

Regression1 <- plm(Y~ X1+ X2 + Control1+ Control2, Database, index = c("ID", "time"), model = "within", effect = "twoways")

I understand how to calculate a classical Mediation in lavaan, but I don't have an idea, how to include the specification of the panel model above. Any suggestions?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: plm Mediation with fixed effects in lavaan
parts: I understand how to calculate a classical Mediation in lavaan, but I don't have an idea, how to include the specification of the panel model above

It looks like plm() takes long-format data, so all the Y observations are in a single column, with another column containing an index for time.  In SEM, panel data are traditionally handled in wide format, like repeated-measures ANOVA (Y on each occasion is in a different column).  Thus, first-order autoregressive paths are specified by regressing Y at T2 on Y at T1, and first-order cross-lagged paths are specified by regressing Y at T2 on X at T1.  Within-time (error) covariance structure is specified by freeing covariances among variables at the same time.

Here is an article that discusses the traditional SEM approach to panel data, illustrated with path diagrams that are easily translated into any software's model syntax (including lavaan):  https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/9c0e/320b78f0d0c110cb6deb3586605a0a687e77.pdf
